0.label: Season Preview
0.title: The Open Era
0.headline: Twenty-one strangers, two tribes, and a rulebook that no longer exists.
paragraphs: Jeff Probst is calling Survivor 51 the start of the Open Era. His words: anything that has ever happened on the show can happen in any season, at any time, in any order, without warning. No theme, no announced twist list, no safe assumptions. Every idol and advantage from fifty previous seasons is back on the table.

That matters more for our pool than it sounds. Idol finds are worth 2, advantages 1, a successful Shot in the Dark 2. A season designed around throwing every mechanic back into the game should have more of those points floating around than a normal year. The castaway who hunts hard may well out-earn the castaway who just wins challenges.

Two tribes for the first time since Winners at War, and 21 players, so one tribe of 11 and one of 10. Two tribes also means one of them loses every single week, which puts roughly half the cast in front of Jeff at any given time. In a three-tribe season your pick can hide for a while. Not this year. Tribe strength is worth more than usual when you draft.

The rest of the shape: 26 days in Fiji, a million dollars to the winner, which is 6 points to whoever holds them. Eleven women and ten men, the first cast to tilt female. Two-hour premiere Wednesday, then 90-minute episodes starting September 30.

Episode 1 is called "Permanent Uncertainty," which is either a mission statement or a warning. It airs Wednesday and earns nobody a single point. Watch it, take notes, then draft. Picks are due 7:00 p.m. Pacific on Wednesday, September 30.

1.title: Permanent Uncertainty
1.headline: Savu takes the first immunity, Toka loses Aaliyah 6-2, and two Shots in the Dark both come up empty.
paragraphs: No points this week, so read this as a scouting report. Tribes are set: Savu has 10 (Alexis, Ana, Carter, Cristian, Eric, Kristin, Linnea, Ori, Rob, Sharonda) and Toka has 11 (Aaliyah, Brady, Devin, Jelly, Jenna, Kilby, Lewis, Maggie, Mike, Patt, Thien An).

Savu won the first immunity challenge and sent Toka to Tribal with Lewis away on Exile. Aaliyah went home 6-2. Brady, Kilby, Maggie, Mike, Patt and Thien An voted together, while Devin and Jelly were the only votes for Jenna.

Aaliyah and Jenna both played their Shot in the Dark and both scrolls read Not Safe, the first time two have misfired at the same Tribal. For drafting purposes that means Jenna's +2 Shot in the Dark is already spent, and Devin and Jelly start the season on the short end of a six-person Toka majority.
Picks are due 7:00 p.m. Pacific on Wednesday, September 30, one hour before Episode 2.

2.title: Weaponized Honesty
2.headline: Toka sweeps both challenges, Jelly finds an idol, Rob tries to vote himself out, and Savu sends Ana home 6-4.
paragraphs: Lewis came back from Exile Island and slotted into Toka in Aaliyah's spot, which evened the tribes at 10 apiece. Over on Toka, Devin laid out his plan for the game, which he called weaponized honesty, and that line gave the episode its title.

The reward was Five Blind Mice, a blindfolded maze run with one caller shouting directions, played for a tarp and pillows. Toka won it. The challenge left marks on both beaches: Kristin hurt her foot and needed a visit from the medical team, and Brady sliced his thumb badly enough that he worried he would be pulled from the game. Production reassured him that people have played on through worse, and he stayed in.

Back at camp, Jelly found Toka's Hidden Immunity Idol. Toka then won immunity too, in a challenge where each tribe drags a heavy dummy through the course as an extra tribe member. That sent Savu to its first Tribal Council of the season.

Savu split into two camps. Ana, Carter, Ori and Rob lined up on Eric, while Alexis, Cristian, Eric, Kristin, Linnea and Sharonda went after Ana. Ana admitted afterward she had made too many promises too early and it caught up with her.

The moment everyone will be talking about: Rob decided Eric deserved a second chance and tried to sacrifice himself, writing his own name on the parchment. A producer had to whisper that you can't vote for yourself. Rob's real vote was never shown. It didn't matter. Ana went home 6-4, the second person out of Survivor 51.

3.title: What I'm Smellin' Is Stinky
3.headline: Rob walks away, Carter misses his boat and becomes a Toka, and the swing votes send Patt home 6-5.
paragraphs: Rob never really recovered from Episode 2, when he tried to write his own name down at Tribal. This week he hurt his foot in the ocean. Medical checked him out and found nothing serious enough to pull him, and Jeff made it clear this was not a medical evacuation. Rob decided to leave anyway. On his way out he quietly handed his Hidden Immunity Idol to Carter.

Then tree mail brought the twist. Each tribe sent one player to visit the other camp. Savu drew rocks and Carter went to Toka, while Devin volunteered to visit Savu. Both visitors learned two things: an advantage was hidden at the camp they were visiting, and they could mutiny and join that tribe for good.

Devin went straight to the water well with Sharonda and pulled a Secret Extra Vote out of the ladle. He told Savu exactly what he'd been offered, then headed home to Toka. Carter's visit went less smoothly. He left his bag at camp, Lewis went through it and found the clue, and Brady took a machete to an oar to get at the advantage. He let Maggie keep the extra vote on one condition: she votes the way he does. Carter, meanwhile, was so busy hunting for that advantage that his boat left without him. He became a member of Toka more or less by accident.

That left Savu with seven against Toka's eleven, and Savu won immunity anyway. Toka built a big lead through the obstacle course but stalled at the puzzle, and Savu came back to win it, along with four egg-laying chickens.

At Toka, Devin, Brady, Jelly, Mike and Patt went after Kilby, which put the vote in the hands of two swing players, Carter and Lewis. Kilby and Maggie floated Mike as their target until Thien An talked them into Patt instead, arguing Mike would be an easy vote later. Carter and Lewis went with that side. Kilby got five votes, Patt got six, and Devin's group lost the numbers for the second vote in a row.

4.title: That's the Magic of Survivor
4.headline: The game splits into three tribes, Dina and Toka stay dry, and Savu blindsides Jenna 4-1.
paragraphs: Jeff teased an early merge, then pulled the rug out with an old school twist. The two tribes became three. Production had planned on three tribes of six, but Rob's exit left Savu one short at five.

The new Dina tribe was Cristian, Eric, Kilby, Lewis, Linnea and Sharonda. Kilby was one of only two original Tokas there and spent his time venting about Devin and the old tribe. He and Eric agreed to have each other's backs almost immediately, though Kilby worried the pairing was too obvious. Lewis was feeling sick, and Eric was ready to cut him loose if Dina lost.

Over at Toka, Kristin was the newcomer and won people over by showing off what she knew about the local fruit. Carter wasn't buying it and wanted her gone. Brady was still sore that Carter and Lewis had flipped on his side at the last vote. Mike tried to patch things up with Thien An, and it didn't land.

The challenge was a relay. Tribes hauled ocean water to fill a container that released a ball, and then two players steered it through a spinning maze. Dina won immunity and a coffee kit. Toka took second and stayed safe, which sent the five-person Savu to Tribal.

At Savu, Jenna sat with three original Tokas: Devin, Jelly and Ori. Alexis told Jenna that Devin had called her untrustworthy, and Jenna passed that straight to Devin, trying to lock in the Toka trio. Then she pitched them on voting out Alexis as the bigger threat. Jelly was open to it, but Devin wasn't sold. At Tribal, Alexis played calm and steady. Jelly, who is quietly holding an idol nobody on her tribe knows about, downplayed her closeness with Ori.

It went the other way. Alexis, Devin, Jelly and Ori all wrote Jenna, and Jenna's lone vote went to Alexis. She left the fourth castaway out of Survivor 51 and said she felt blindsided. Jeff noted that all four people voted out so far have been women.

5.title: Not Here to Get a Pedicure
5.headline: Toka wins immunity, two tribes go to Tribal, Savu sends Alexis home 3-1, and a deadlock ends Linnea's game.
paragraphs: Toka found a note at camp saying one of them was needed somewhere else. The draw picked Maggie, who went off on a journey and came back with an Alliance Builder Extra Vote, an extra vote she could hand to a player on another tribe. She gave it to Kilby. Maggie already had the Extra Vote she won in Episode 3, and that one went to Lewis.

Immunity was a dive-and-throw challenge. Players swam out for buoys one at a time, carried them across a balance beam, and a thrower tossed them into three baskets. Mike threw for Toka, Sharonda for Dina and Ori for Savu. Dina and Savu were so slow that Mike was the only thrower who got a real shot, and Toka won immunity plus a basket of pastries. Dina and Savu both went to Tribal.

At Savu, the four left were Alexis, Devin, Jelly and Ori. Devin, Jelly and Ori have been together since day one as the Helicopter Alliance. Alexis tried to pull Jelly away from Devin, and Jelly said she felt stuck in the middle. In the end Ori stayed with his oldest alliance, and Alexis went home 3-1.

Dina was the wild one. Lewis gave Sharonda a ring and told her it was a blood idol that would become real if they both survived two Tribals. Cristian, who said he knows jewelry, saw through it right away. At the vote, Lewis and Kilby played their two extra votes on Linnea, while Cristian, Eric, Linnea and Sharonda all wrote Lewis. That made it 4-4. The revote tied again, which sent it to deadlock: Cristian, Eric, Kilby and Sharonda had to agree on Lewis or Linnea, or draw rocks. Kilby would not budge, so the other three went along, and Linnea was voted out. Jeff called it historic.

For the pool: Toka's six (Brady, Carter, Kristin, Maggie, Mike and Thien An) pick up half a point each for immunity. Maggie also gets +1 for winning the Alliance Builder Extra Vote on her journey. The point goes to whoever wins an advantage, not to whoever ends up casting it, so Kilby and Lewis get nothing for the extra votes they played. Alexis was on ten rosters, which makes her the most-drafted castaway out of the game so far.

6.title: I Love Crying
6.headline: Kristin takes a tethered idol off Exile, Toka and Dina stay safe, and Savu sends Ori home after his Shot in the Dark misses.
paragraphs: Tree mail called one player from each tribe to a Summit: Sharonda for Dina, Ori for Savu and Kristin for Toka. Two of them would go back to camp as heroes with food, and one would stay on Exile. Kristin volunteered for Exile. Ori and Sharonda headed home with a lunch of ribs and corn.

Kristin's night on Exile came with a Tethered Idol. Only she can play it, and only on Ori or Sharonda, before the final five. If she is still in the game after both of them are gone, it turns into a regular idol she can play on herself. Jeff called her a fan favorite who has applied for 25 years and is now playing on a broken foot with a powerful advantage. Sharonda told Dina about the food but not the idol.

Toka had its own drama. Maggie spent time on the swing instead of the fire and then turned the tribe's hammock into a fishing net, which Brady did not appreciate. He and Mike were also getting on each other's nerves, and Mike started talking about working with Kristin. At Dina, Eric was still stung that Kilby had sided with Lewis at the last vote, and Cristian started thinking about joining Kilby and Lewis himself.

The immunity challenge had players untangle themselves from ropes, drag sandbags, knock puzzle pieces loose and then solve the puzzle. Savu led early behind Ori's sandbag work but fell apart at the puzzle. Toka and Dina finished seconds apart, and Savu went to Tribal for the third week in a row.

That left Devin, Jelly and Ori, all three from the Helicopter Alliance. Jelly let it be known she has an idol and would not vote out Devin, her closest ally. Ori teared up before the vote and played his Shot in the Dark, but it came up Not Safe. Devin and Jelly voted him out 2-0.

For the pool: Toka and Dina each get half a point per person for immunity. Kristin gets +1 for the Exile advantage, which makes her the top castaway this week with 1.5 and puts her at 3 points for the season. Ori's missed Shot in the Dark scores nothing. Kristin is on fifteen rosters, more than anyone else, so that point lands almost everywhere. Ori was on nine, and four of those also lost Alexis last week.
